brief: The 10-year Treasury yield broke out of a three-year range to two-decade highs, and MOVE (bond volatility) exploded alongside it, opening a gap versus the SPX; the note argues equities care about the speed of the rates move, not just its level, and flags 5.2% then 5.5% as the next levels to watch. Small caps (IWM) are underperforming QQQ as yields rise, yet VIX has not reacted to the bond-vol spike. That calm faces a test as S&P 500 buyback-blackout coverage climbs from 64% (as of 9/21) toward roughly 490 corporates by mid-October and about 85% by week-end, removing the market's price-insensitive bid just as CTAs position to sell. Separately, crowded speculative WTI longs (93rd percentile gross, 85th percentile net after short covering) were flushed by a 10.2% five-session plunge in November WTI as Saudi Arabia repaired its East-West pipeline, some oil flowed through Hormuz, and US-Iran talks showed progress; oil volatility stayed calm through the swing, so the note prefers cheap options over chasing spot. SPX itself is range-bound since May, favoring a mean-reversion mindset over chasing momentum.
